boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Bull's Gap record (November 11-13, 1864), the only frozen record in Breckenridge's Advance into East Tennessee [November 1864]. The frozen interval covers the attacks at Bull's Gap on the 11th and 12th and the firing of the 13th. The Union evacuation on the night of the 13th, the night attack and rout near Russellville and Morristown on the 14th, and the operations at Strawberry Plains (16th-17th) are context; their losses and captures are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Gillem's Governor's Guard brigade and gives the Confederate department force as approx. 2,400 (side bound 2,400); the live field reads '0 total (US ; CS ;)'. Breckinridge says he advanced with a miscellaneous force of about 1,800 men and six howitzers, later joined by Palmer's mixed force of some 600 (read 'GOO' in OCR), against an enemy of about 2,500 with six guns. Gillem says he learned Breckinridge was advancing with a force much superior to his, that Ammen told others the attackers were just 1,200, and that at Morristown on the 14th the enemy numbered probably 2,500 to 3,000.
claims.rationale: Each commander's figure for his own side and estimates of the other, at different dates; Gillem gives no count of his own brigade in the selected report. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live blank is not measured absence.

claims.value: Gillem says he posted his troops at the gap for defense front and rear and strengthened the position with the few axes he had; the assault of the 12th reached the rude works on the ridges of his left. Breckinridge says his dismounted force ascended the mountain to move down on the enemy's left and carried a line of works, and that he later turned the gap through Taylor's Gap, two and a half miles below.
claims.rationale: Ground and works described by the two commanders; no map verification. The works were thrown up on the 10th, so the phase is left unresolved.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Gillem says the attacks of the 11th and 12th, including Vaughn's attack on his rear, were repulsed, and that he evacuated the gap on the night of the 13th for want of bread, ammunition and forage. Breckinridge says his force on the mountain carried a line of works but the assault as a whole did not succeed, and that on the evening of the 11th his opponent's rearguard had been driven into the gap. The frozen description dates the withdrawal 'after midnight on the 4th'.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The Union withdrawal, not a successful assault, ended the frozen interval; the result field is kept. The frozen description's '4th' is inconsistent with the frozen dates and is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty field reads 'Total unknown (US 241; CS unknown)'; the live field reads 424 (US 324; CS 100). For the frozen interval Gillem reports only enemy dead: 27 left in front of his lines on the 12th and 1 captain and 8 privates after Vaughn's rear attack. His loss in the retreat of the 14th (6 guns, 61 wagons read 'G1', 71 ambulances, about 300 horses and probably about 150 men) and Breckinridge's about 300 prisoners in the night attack belong to the context action.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. No inspected source gives the frozen Union 241 or the live figures; the retreat losses are outside the interval and are not added.

open_questions: Thomas's No. 1 relay of Gillem's November 15 telegram and Ammen's No. 2 dispatches (read, not selected), Vaughn's, Duke's, Palmer's and Tool's reports (Nos. 5-8), returns and maps remain deferred. Breckinridge's November 17 dispatch, selected with his report, concerns Strawberry Plains and is context only. The NPS page's Description field is empty, so the frozen Arnold description stands for the NPS/CWSAC narrative.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page, whose description is empty, plus the frozen Arnold rows). Alvan C. Gillem's November 16, 1864 report to Governor Johnson (Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIX, Part 1, No. 3) is one family of interested Union accounts, written after the rout and blaming Ammen. John C. Breckinridge's November 17 dispatch and November 29 report (No. 4) are one family of interested Confederate accounts, the same author family as his registered Baton Rouge report and his Southwestern Virginia report. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness; report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
